quickSummary: At the G1/S restriction point, CDK phosphorylation of Retinoblastoma (Rb) releases E2F to activate S-phase genes. DNA damage triggers ATM/ATR kinases to stabilize p53, inducing p21 to inhibit Cyclin E-CDK2 and arrest the cycle. At the Spindle Assembly Checkpoint (SAC), once all kinetochores are attached under tension, active APC/C targets Securin for proteasomal destruction, freeing Separase to cleave Cohesin rings and initiate Anaphase.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.2 The $G_1/S$ Restriction Switch (Rb / E2F)
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 The $G_1/S$ Restriction Switch (Rb / E2F)

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Rb inhibits E2F. CDK phosphorylation releases E2F to transcribe S-phase genes. p53 induces p21 to stop CDKs upon DNA damage. APC/C destroys Securin to activate Separase.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
Rb / E2F MOLECULAR RESTRICTION SWITCH
                     
   Unphosphorylated Rb ──[Binds & Inhibits]──► E2F Factor (S-Phase Genes OFF)
                                    │
   Cyclin D/E-CDK4/2 ──[Phosphorylates Rb]──► Hyper-phosphorylated Rb Detaches
                                    │
   Free E2F Factor ──► Activates Transcription of S-Phase Genes (DNA Polymerase, Histones)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• In quiescent or early $G_1$ cells, unphosphorylated **Retinoblastoma ($\text{Rb}$)** binds to the $\text{E2F}$ transcription factor and suppresses its activity.
• Growth factor mitogens activate Cyclin D-CDK4/6 and Cyclin E-CDK2, which **hyper-phosphorylate $\text{Rb}$**, forcing it to dissociate from $\text{E2F}$. Free $\text{E2F}$ drives the transcription of DNA polymerases, thymidine kinase, and histone proteins.

conceptBreakdown.heading: The p53 DNA Damage Checkpoint Cascade
conceptBreakdown.title: The p53 DNA Damage Checkpoint Cascade
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
p53 DNA DAMAGE CASCADE
                        
   DNA Damage ──► ATM/ATR Kinases ──► Stabilizes p53 ──► Transcribes p21 (CDK Inhibitor)
                                                                 │
   Cell Cycle Arrest at G₁/S ◄── Inactivates Cyclin E-CDK2 ──────┘
conceptBreakdown.content:
• DNA double-strand breaks activate sensor kinases (**ATM/ATR**), which phosphorylate and stabilize **$\text{p53}$ ('Guardian of the Genome')**.
• Active $\text{p53}$ transactivates **$\text{p21}^{\text{CIP1/WAF1}}$**, a stoichiometric CDK inhibitor that blocks Cyclin E-CDK2, arresting the cycle at $G_1/S$ to allow repair. If damage is irreparable, $\text{p53}$ initiates **Apoptosis**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Spindle Assembly Checkpoint (SAC) & APC/C
conceptBreakdown.title: Spindle Assembly Checkpoint (SAC) & APC/C
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
APC/C ANAPHASE CASCADE
                           
   Active APC/C ──► Ubiquitinates SECURIN ──► Releases Active SEPARASE
                                                       │
   Anaphase Onset ◄── Cleaves COHESIN Rings ──────────┘
conceptBreakdown.content:
• Unattached kinetochores recruit MAD2/BUBR1 proteins to generate a **'WAIT-Anaphase'** inhibitory signal.
• Once all chromosomes achieve bipolar spindle attachment under mechanical tension at the metaphase plate, SAC is silenced, activating the **Anaphase-Promoting Complex / Cyclosome (APC/C)**.
• APC/C ubiquitinates **Securin**, causing its degradation. This unmasks active **Separase** protease, which cleaves the **Cohesin** rings holding sister chromatids together, triggering synchronous anaphase onset.
